children: Turkey's central bank left its key interest rate at 37% on Thursday, as expected, keeping it unchanged for a fifth consecutive meeting as it continues to monitor the inflation impact of the Iran war.
In a Reuters poll, sixteen of 17 economists in a Reuters poll forecast the policy rate would remain at 37%, while one expected a 100 basis-point cut.

The central bank also did not adjust its overnight lending and borrowing rates from 40% and 35.5%, respectively. The bank uses the rate corridor to adjust the cost of funding to the market when necessary without changing the benchmark rate.

Last month, central bank resumed one-week repo auctions, which have been suspended since March in order to control the inflationary impact of the Iran war. Overnight interest rate  which had remained at around 40% since the suspension, fell by 300 basis points.
The war-related surge in energy prices has rattled import-reliant economies like Turkey, where inflation was 31.51% last month.
In the latest inflation report, the central bank raised its inflation forecast for the end of 2026 to 28% from 26%. The government sees inflation to stand at 28.4% at the end of this year.
Economists continued to expect monetary easing over the remainder of the year but are closely monitoring new tensions in the region and its impact on inflation.
